A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAEE and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Shared methods and experiments can be matched across renaming, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original performance, latency, retrieval sensitivity, and exiting-layer results across eight classification tasks.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds backbone evaluations, a database-filtering ablation, construction-cost measurements, fine-tuned comparisons, and retrieval examples.

M1.justification: The database-building pseudocode replaces max(logits) with max(softmax(logits)) in Algorithm 2.1 versus Algorithm B.1. This locally corrects the documented confidence computation; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed. The core retrieval and exit-selection procedure remains.

E1.justification: Both versions use SST-2, SST-5, MR, CR, MPQA, SUBJ, TREC, and CoLA. The added backbones, filtered-database experiment, and fine-tuning comparisons reuse these tasks without introducing another data domain or task requirement.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds T5-Large, Llama-3-8B, Gemma-7B, DeeBERT, CALM, and SLEB as evaluated comparators. Appendix G additionally evaluates FREE. The original comparators remain; LM-BFF is renamed RoBERTa-Large rather than removed.

E3.justification: v2 adds T5, Llama, and Gemma configurations and A100-based evaluations. New protocols include 50-epoch DeeBERT off-ramp training, removing four SLEB blocks, one-epoch CALM/FREE fine-tuning, and a filtered-database control. The original task metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds an ablation testing whether database examples misclassified by the full backbone explain RAEE's accuracy gains. Appendices F and I add construction-cost analysis and two retrieval case studies, while exiting-depth analysis expands across backbones. The original top-k and database-size analyses remain; separate encoding/retrieving timing detail is lost.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark performance. Figure 2's boxplots describe neighboring examples' probabilities and are retained without a changed uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 performance values remain unchanged, including RAEE's 63.27 average. v2 adds extensive results: RAEE-Llama averages 58.52 and RAEE-Gemma 54.41; the separate Table 2 ablation reports RAEE at 63.39 versus RAEE w/o at 56.61. New latency plots show that speedups over full T5 and Llama backbones are not consistent.

T1.justification: Equation 4 adds an explicit sum over each neighbor's candidate exiting layers, resolving the previously unbound candidate index and explaining that only one matching layer contributes. This is a local mathematical correction; no new theorem, proof, or guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list replace explicit state-of-the-art performance claims with robust zero-shot performance. The central contributions—distribution approximation through retrieved exiting information and improved inference efficiency—remain. Training-free operation is still described despite its removal from the title.

C2.justification: v2 introduces database-based error correction as the explanation for outperforming full-depth prediction, supported by the new ablation. Appendix G acknowledges that fine-tuned CALM/FREE achieve higher average performance at additional training cost. The latency explanation now emphasizes late exits. The original limitations are retained verbatim in Appendix J.

D1.justification: v2 discloses LM-BFF split alignment, earliest-layer tie-breaking, selectable backbone-state embeddings, baseline training/block-removal settings, and A100 hardware. Appendix F supplies database entry counts, storage sizes, and construction times. Conversely, v1's maximum sequence length of 512 and CPU/main-memory specifications disappear. The code-access pointer is unchanged.

R1.justification: References are added for T5, Llama 3, Gemma, CALM, SLEB, and a retrieval-augmentation survey. The introduction more explicitly positions RAEE against accuracy-sacrificing early exiting. Most related-work discussion and its distinction from generation-focused retrieval remain unchanged after relocation to Appendix H.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: algorithms, exiting-layer analysis, related work, and limitations move into appendices, while the main experiments center on the new accuracy explanation. The abstract, contributions, and results narrative are revised, and the title changes from Training-Free to Robust.

P2.justification: Table 1 changes from paired performance/latency rows to an expanded performance-only table, with latency presented in new multipanel Figures 3–4. The exiting-layer table expands and moves to the appendix. New ablation, construction-cost, fine-tuning, and example tables substantially change the presentation; the original three-process latency table disappears.

improvement.justification: v2's targeted ablation, construction-cost measurements, and broader comparisons improve support for v1's largely unexplained accuracy gains and practical feasibility. However, the claimed consistent acceleration conflicts with Figures 3–4, which show slower T5 and several Llama cases, while replacing numerical timing tables with plots loses detail. These tradeoffs support a limited net improvement.
